group.title: Food and time
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: The first meal of the day.
wrong: Breakfast is the meal we eat at midnight.

words.meaning: The main meal of the day, usually in the evening.
examples: We have {dinner} with our family at six.
wrong: Dinner is the first meal of the morning.

words.meaning: A hot brown drink made from beans.
examples: He drinks a cup of {coffee} every morning.
wrong: Coffee is a cold white food you cut with a knife.

words.meaning: A white drink that comes from cows.
examples: The children drink a glass of {milk} at breakfast.
wrong: Milk is a hard yellow stone.

words.meaning: A food made from flour and baked in an oven.
wrong: Bread is a drink made from fruit.

words.meaning: Small white or brown grains that people cook and eat.
examples: We eat {rice} with fish for dinner.
wrong: Rice is a very cold drink.

words.meaning: A sweet food that grows on trees or plants, such as an apple.
wrong: Fruit is a kind of meat from a cow.

words.meaning: An oval food that comes from a hen.
examples: I had a boiled {egg} for breakfast.
wrong: An egg is a vegetable that grows under the ground.

words.meaning: An animal that lives in water, or the meat of this animal.
wrong: A fish is an animal that lives only on mountains.

words.meaning: A food made from milk, often yellow or white.
wrong: Cheese is a drink we pour into a glass.

words.meaning: A sweet white food that you put in tea or cakes.
examples: Do you want {sugar} in your tea?
wrong: Sugar is a salty food that comes from the sea.

words.meaning: A white powder used to give food flavor.
examples: Add a little {salt} to the soup.
wrong: Salt is a sweet drink.

words.meaning: A plant that you eat, such as a carrot.
wrong: A vegetable is a large animal.

words.meaning: Having a high temperature.
examples: The soup is very {hot}, so be careful.
wrong: The ice is hot and makes my hand freeze.

words.meaning: Having a low temperature.
examples: I need a coat because it is {cold} outside.
wrong: The soup is cold and burns my tongue.

words.meaning: Not big in size.
wrong: An elephant is a very small animal.

words.meaning: Not old; made or bought a short time ago.
wrong: My new shoes are twenty years old.

words.meaning: Having lived or existed for a long time.
wrong: The new baby is eighty years old.

words.meaning: A period of seven days.
wrong: A week has twelve days.

words.meaning: One of the twelve parts of a year, such as May.
wrong: A month has seven hours.

words.meaning: A period of twelve months.
wrong: A year has seven days.

words.meaning: The early part of the day, before noon.
wrong: The morning is the dark part of the day after midnight.

words.meaning: The part of the day between the afternoon and night.
wrong: The evening is the time when the sun is highest.

words.meaning: The time of day when it is dark.
wrong: Night is the time when the sun is very high.

words.meaning: On this day.
wrong: I met her today last Friday.

words.meaning: On the day after today.
wrong: I went to the beach tomorrow last year.

words.meaning: On the day before today.
wrong: I will go to the shop yesterday.

words.meaning: Every time; at all times.
wrong: I always eat lunch only on Mondays.

words.meaning: At no time; not ever.
wrong: I never go to school, and I go every day.

words.meaning: Many times; frequently.
wrong: I often go to the beach one time in my whole life.

words.meaning: To move something so that it is not closed.
wrong: I open the door by closing it.

words.meaning: To shut something.
examples: Please {close} the window; it is cold.
wrong: I close the door by opening it wide.

words.meaning: To begin to do something.
wrong: The film starts after it ends.

words.meaning: To come to the end of something.
examples: I will {finish} my homework before dinner.
wrong: I finish my work before I begin it.

words.meaning: To take liquid into your mouth and swallow it.
examples: I {drink} a glass of water every morning.
wrong: I drink a piece of bread with a fork.

words.meaning: To move on foot at a normal speed.
wrong: I walk to school by plane in five minutes.

words.meaning: To move on foot very quickly.
wrong: I run to the shop very slowly and sit down all day.

words.meaning: To take part in a game or to make music.
examples: The boys {play} football in the park.
wrong: I play a book with a pencil.

words.meaning: To look at words and understand them.
examples: I {read} a book before I sleep.
wrong: I read a book with my ears only.

words.meaning: To stay in a place until something happens.
wrong: I wait for the bus by leaving at once.
